item.title: Sade Skips Rock Hall Ceremony But Sends Thanks To Supporters
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Sade won't attend this weekend's Rock Hall celebration, but the band shares its gratitude and remembers collaborator Mike Pela.
item.content:encoded:
Sade won’t be in the room when the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame honors the band this weekend.

Instead, the four musicians are marking the moment with a message to everyone who’s kept their music close.

The group confirmed the decision in a statement on its official website, without explaining why they can’t attend. Sade, Stuart Matthewman, Andrew Hale and Paul Denman signed the note together, making clear that missing the ceremony doesn’t diminish their appreciation.

“Please know that our absence takes nothing away from how much this recognition means to us,” the band wrote. Their thanks extended beyond the people who voted them in to the listeners who’ve made room for their songs.

That recognition covers a partnership that began in London in 1982 and has kept the same four members throughout. Sade’s voice sits alongside Matthewman’s saxophone and guitar, Hale’s keyboards and Denman’s bass across a catalog that has reached several generations.

Six studio albums have sold more than 50 million copies, with Diamond Life launching the group in 1984. The debut also earned them a Best New Artist Grammy, starting a run that later brought Love Deluxe and Lovers Rock.

Hip-Hop’s affection for that music has often taken a very personal form. Drake commissioned a nearly nine-foot sculpture inspired by Love Deluxe earlier this year, with artist Rebecca Maria spending six months shaping it by hand.

For their own tribute, Sade made sure longtime collaborators shared in the recognition. The statement thanked manager Roger Davies and dedicated the honor to producer and engineer Mike Pela, who died in 2022.

The ceremony takes place Saturday, November 14, at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater.

item.title: Usher & Chris Brown Cancel December 6 Miami Show As Two Dates Remain
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Usher and Chris Brown canceled a Miami date after earlier cuts, despite a reported $284.7 million gross through October 3.
item.content:encoded:
Usher and Chris Brown are leaving South Florida fans with two December dates after their third Hard Rock Stadium show was canceled.

The December 6 concert in Miami Gardens is canceled, while tickets for December 3 and December 5 remain available.

Ticketmaster’s event notice confirms the change but doesn’t explain why this particular performance was scrapped. “Unfortunately, the Event Organizer has had to cancel your event. You don’t need to do a thing.”

That follows the November 16 cancellation at SoFi Stadium, although the November 15 Inglewood show remains listed for sale.

Neither cancellation notice establishes that a disagreement between the singers caused these latest changes.

The itinerary had already lost four October stops before this latest round of cancellations.

Baltimore on October 17, Cincinnati on October 24, Columbia on October 29 and Indianapolis on October 31 were removed, with organizers citing the health and well-being of the touring party and crew.

That explanation applied to October, not automatically to the two newly canceled performances.

The canceled dates haven’t erased what the joint tour has already achieved at the box office.

Usher and Brown became the first co-headliners to lead Billboard’s monthly Top Tours ranking, a chart that started in 2019. September topped both the revenue and ticket-sales rankings for that month, even though the tour’s July and August grosses were higher.

Their record-setting September brought in $77.4 million from 423,000 tickets across 10 shows, according to Billboard Boxscore. Through the October 3 stop in El Paso, the first 36 reported concerts had generated $284.7 million and sold more than 1.5 million tickets.

Those numbers measure reported ticket grosses, not the amount either singer personally took home. They’re figures through October 3, rather than a final total accounting for every performance remaining on the itinerary.

For South Florida ticket buyers, the immediate distinction is which date appears on their order.

Live Nation still lists both remaining Hard Rock Stadium performances with tickets available for 7 P.M., even as December 6 carries a cancellation label.

The current itinerary also retains November 20 and November 21 in New Orleans before December 11 and December 12 in Tampa.

item.title: Jamaican Government Denies Cardi B Canceled Concert Claims As Drama Becomes International Crisis
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Cardi B's canceled Kingston booking draws a government denial as Jamaica says it never promised to cover concert costs.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B is getting pushback from Jamaica’s government over claims it could help cover costs for her canceled concert.

The dispute now extends beyond her payment fight with BZR WKND promoter Ryan Burke to who was supposed to cover the bill.

Jamaica’s Ministry of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport said Tuesday that no government money had been paid or committed toward appearance fees or other concert costs.

Its statement, reported by The Jamaica Star, described the event as “a private commercial engagement in which the Government was not involved.”

“The Government of Jamaica made no commitment or payment towards appearance fees or any fees whatsoever, in relation to a proposed concert in Jamaica which was expected to feature international recording artist, Cardi B,” the ministry said.

That response follows Cardi’s claim that the government was willing to cover outstanding production expenses to rescue the performance. The ministry’s denial concerns public funding, while Cardi and Burke still have competing accounts of their own financial arrangement.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Burke maintained that Cardi received her full $2.5 million fee and said he wanted the money returned. Cardi disputed that figure during her November 9 Instagram Live and said she received a $1 million deposit.

Cardi blamed the failed show on production money that didn’t arrive when it was needed and threatened to countersue if Burke sued her. Her scheduled October 18 appearance at Kingston’s National Stadium had been promoted as the centerpiece of Cardi B & Friends.

“It was so much that even the Jamaica government was trying to make it so right that they was willing to pay the rest,” Cardi B fumed in an IG live. “I was just like, you know what? It’s just too much. Like everything was just It just turned me off.”

The show’s August launch had included Cardi’s manager Kelvin Santiago and promoter Gramps Morgan, with Culture Minister Olivia Grange also attending.

Tuesday’s statement separates that public involvement from any commitment to finance it.

The ministry also said Jamaica’s current spending priorities are hurricane recovery and reconstruction, limiting what it can spend on entertainment events.

It said Prime Minister Andrew Holness had directed funds toward recovery wherever possible, even before his more recent expenditure directives.

Cardi’s representatives have directed ticketing questions to the promoters and future performance announcements to the rapper’s own official channels.

item.title: PlaqueBoyMax Hands Matt Proxy $25,000 After Rising Star Finale
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: PlaqueBoyMax picks Matt Proxy for the Rising Star title after a three-day contest, with cash and studio access on the line.
item.content:encoded:
PlaqueBoyMax turned Matt Proxy’s weekend in Los Angeles into a five-figure payday after naming him his first Rising Star winner. The Minneapolis rapper collected $25,000 at the November 8 finale at The Belasco after six contestants spent a weekend making music together.

The streamer had put stage presence at the center of his judging before anyone collected the prize.

Red Bull partnered on the three-day competition, which placed emerging artists in a shared house while viewers followed their work.

A 90-minute songwriting and performance challenge was part of the schedule, alongside a label meeting and a timed styling assignment at Wasteland. Wiz Khalifa, Coi Leray and Lil Yachty were among the celebrity guests who offered critiques as the contestants worked through their assignments.

The artists weren’t only competing for attention from celebrity guests and the people inside the venue. Online voting helped determine their rankings, with Tana entering the final day on 13 stars and Matt Proxy just behind him on 12.

Both rappers ultimately led the voting after their performances, and PlaqueBoyMax asked the room to respond before announcing his winner. Raud, Hawsa, Boohavinn and Earfzilla also performed in the finale, which reached viewers through Twitch and YouTube.

Matt Proxy arrived with a recording career already underway, not an empty catalog. His June project trojan horse featured Current Joys and fakemink, and his music mixed live instrumentation with the Hip-Hop influences he’d grown up hearing in Minneapolis.

The win follows a New York headline show where he performed the project for an audience already familiar with his music. Onstage at the Rising Star finale, he also asked the audience to sit down for a tribute to his late sister.

For PlaqueBoyMax, the contest comes as his music streams receive recognition beyond his channel. He’s among the nominees for Best Music Streamer at the 2026 Streamer Awards, alongside DDG, Bishu and AriAtHome.

Matt Proxy’s prize also includes access to Red Bull Music Studios in Los Angeles.

item.title: Rochelle Fleming Dies At 72, Leaving First Choice’s Mark On Hip-Hop Soul
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Rochelle Fleming died at 72, leaving First Choice records that reached Mary J. Blige, Kaytranada and new waves of R&B and dance fans.
item.content:encoded:
Rochelle Fleming, the First Choice singer whose records reached new fans through Mary J. Blige and Kaytranada, died at 72.

She died November 5 in Philadelphia. Her manager, George Iz Correia, shared the news on behalf of her family. No cause of death was announced.

BMG paid tribute to Fleming on November 9, pointing to the remixes and samples that kept her group’s songs in use long after their first release. The company represents part of First Choice’s catalog through Salsoul.

“Rochelle was a remarkable singer, and the records she made with First Choice have had a lasting influence on dance music,” BMG executive Dan Baxter said.

For fans of Hip-Hop soul, one route back to First Choice runs through Blige. She closed her 1999 album Mary with a cover of “Let No Man Put Asunder.” The song came from First Choice’s 1977 album Delusions, which also held “Doctor Love.”

The track had found a second life well before Blige sang it. First Choice broke up in 1980, but a 1983 remix of “Let No Man Put Asunder” helped renew interest in the group’s work. Club DJs kept drawing on the song as house music grew.

A different First Choice record reached listeners through Kaytranada.

He sampled “Love Thang” on “10%,” his 2019 song with Kali Uchis from the album Bubba. The track went on to win Best Dance Recording at the 2021 Grammy Awards.

Those later records drew from a group rooted in Philadelphia’s teen music scene. Fleming and her school friends first sang as the Debonettes before adopting the name First Choice. Their first record under that name, “This Is the House (Where Love Died),” came out in 1972.

A year later, “Armed and Extremely Dangerous” reached No. 11 on the R&B chart and No. 28 on the pop chart. Producer Norman Harris helped shape their early sound and worked with the group as it moved to Gold Mind, a label linked to Salsoul.

First Choice made six albums before the split. Fleming kept recording on her own, including the 1985 single “Love Itch,” while the group’s old songs kept resurfacing on new records.

item.title: SZA & Daddy Yankee Lead Coachella 2027 As Full Lineup Arrives
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: SZA and Daddy Yankee take top billing as Coachella confirms its 2027 performers and puts another pass sale on the calendar.
item.content:encoded:
SZA has her Coachella headlining spot locked in, with Daddy Yankee joining the top of the festival’s 2027 bill. The newly announced lineup puts her on Sunday and gives the reggaeton star a separate top-billed production.

Dua Lipa takes Friday and Tame Impala takes Saturday across the two weekends. The festival returns to Indio, California, April 9-11 and April 16-18, giving each headliner two dates.

For SZA, the announcement turns weeks of booking reports into an actual festival commitment. AllHipHop previously covered her trip to Tahiti to keep working on new music while those Coachella talks were still circulating, with no album title or release date attached.

She’s already shared that festival’s stage with some familiar collaborators before getting this headline slot. SZA brought Kendrick Lamar into her 2018 set and returned as Justin Bieber’s surprise guest in April 2026 to perform “Snooze,” putting another Coachella appearance between her own bookings.

This time, her Sunday bill also includes Don Toliver and Becky G alongside Dom Dolla, Kygo and The Neighbourhood. Friday brings its own R&B draw with Leon Thomas and Kehlani, while Madonna, JISOO and Zara Larsson are also listed for that day.

Saturday’s schedule spans another set of sounds, with Phoebe Bridgers, Weezer, Tiesto, Martin Garrix and Role Model. Daddy Yankee’s separate top billing adds another major name beyond those three nightly headliners, though the announcement doesn’t spell out his production details.

The new bill follows a 2026 edition headlined by Justin Bieber, Sabrina Carpenter, Karol G and Anyma. Karol G became the first Latina solo artist to headline the festival’s main stage that year, making Daddy Yankee’s newly announced place on the 2027 bill another major Latin booking for the desert event.

People watching from home will still have a way in on both weekends through YouTube’s exclusive livestream.

The platform’s partnership with Goldenvoice now runs through 2030, and April 2027 marks 15 years of bringing Coachella to online audiences worldwide.

The festival’s official website lists the next pass sale for Friday, November 13, at noon Pacific.

item.title: Megan Thee Stallion Brings Denise Back To Reggie Dinkins
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion announces her return as Denise in season two of The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins on NBC.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion is bringing Denise back to The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins, announcing her season-two return in a new Instagram post.

The Houston rapper shared the update Tuesday, November 10, putting her character back in the conversation after a first-season appearance opposite Daniel Radcliffe as filmmaker Arthur Tobin. The NBC comedy stars Tracy Morgan as a former football player trying to rebuild his reputation.

"Guess who's on my mind phone againnn🧙‍♂️🪄😂 DENISE IS BACK 😘," Megan wrote in her Instagram announcement. Her caption also directed viewers to the show's Monday broadcasts on NBC and next-day streaming on Peacock.

The post pairs a clip of Megan in a red dress with audio labeled "Thin Ice." She adds wizard emojis to her announcement about Denise.

Denise is a divorced mother and mail carrier whose interest in Tobin gave Megan a chance to play against Radcliffe in the comedy. AllHipHop covered her introduction to the series when NBC first unveiled the role earlier this year.

Morgan had already praised the rapper's approach to the job during a February 23 interview with TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle. Asked about working with Megan, he focused on how comfortable she was on set.

"She is so great. She's not just a rapper, she played the mailman, so she was down to earth. She was cool," Morgan said. "And I love that because she was so down to earth. She's grounded. That's what I can say about Megan Thee Stallion, she's grounded."

The interview also laid out the comedy's central setup: Morgan's disgraced athlete lets a documentary crew follow him as he attempts to repair his public image. Radcliffe plays the filmmaker caught up in that comeback effort.

Megan's return adds another television credit to a run that already includes P-Valley, where she appeared as Tina Snow, and She-Hulk: Attorney at Law, where she played herself. Her screen work also includes D####: The Musical and the 2024 Mean Girls film.

Erika Alexander, Bobby Moynihan, Precious Way and Jalyn Hall also star in The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins. Megan's new post confirms that Denise will be part of its second season.

item.title: Yella Beezy Jury Starts Deliberations Wednesday After Final MO3 Arguments
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Yella Beezy's MO3 trial reaches its verdict phase as lawyers finish their arguments and jurors prepare to weigh the case.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy must wait another night before jurors begin deciding his fate in the MO3 murder case. Closing arguments ended Tuesday with prosecutors demanding a conviction and his attorneys arguing the state hadn’t proved its case.

The Dallas County panel’s first assignment was choosing a foreperson rather than debating guilt. According to FOX4’s courtroom coverage, the judge told jurors not to discuss the case yet and sent them home ahead of Wednesday’s deliberations.

Prosecutor Tommy Adams tied the alleged plot to a feud with MO3 and pointed jurors toward phone contacts and a disputed $40,000 withdrawal.

Adams argued that meetings involving Yella Beezy and Jerry Johnson were followed by calls to Kewon White. He also pointed to cell phone records showing 15 calls between Johnson and White during the rapper’s 57-hour return trip to North Texas.

Defense attorney John Gussio pushed back against treating gaps as proof.

“It’s not your job to put the pieces in the puzzle. It’s not your job to interpret language and text. It’s not your job to speculate,” Gussio told jurors during his closing argument.

He also challenged the idea that the two rappers’ music established a murder motive.

“There’s no motive to do anything to each other. They were making money,” Gussio said, arguing that artistic material shouldn’t substitute for evidence against his client.

The fight over cash has already occupied a substantial stretch of testimony.

During the defense’s earlier challenge to the payment theory, Detective Eric Barnes acknowledged investigators couldn’t trace recovered cash directly to Yella Beezy’s bank withdrawal.

That transaction occurred November 20, 2020, nine days after MO3’s killing on Interstate 35. The defense also pointed to other large withdrawals and questioned whether the money simply reflected the rapper’s regular spending habits.

Yella Beezy has pleaded not guilty and denied involvement in the killing. Prosecutors accuse him of paying Kewon White to carry it out, while White was separately convicted of capital murder in September.

The jury is due back at 9 A.M. Wednesday to begin deliberations.

item.title: Usher & Chris Brown Scrap November 16 SoFi Show As Refund Notices Arrive
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Usher and Chris Brown lose their second SoFi date as ticket buyers receive refund notices, but Sunday's show stays listed.
item.content:encoded:
Usher and Chris Brown ticket holders are getting refund notices instead of a second night at SoFi Stadium. Their Monday, November 16 concert in Inglewood has been canceled, while the November 15 show remains on the calendar.

A ticket holder’s Ticketmaster account supplied the clearest sign of the change, according to TMZ, which obtained a screenshot showing the event marked “CANCELED.” Buyers received notice that their money would be refunded.

The surviving Sunday date matters for anyone trying to figure out whether the entire Los Angeles stop is gone. Live Nation’s current tour listing still advertises November 15 at SoFi, with no November 16 performance among its upcoming shows.

That change comes as the pair deal with refund demands over their first Atlanta concert, a different problem involving a show that actually happened. Ticket holders complained that the November 5 performance started around 10 P.M. instead of its advertised 7:30 P.M. start.

Their complaints weren’t only about waiting, because the two headliners also performed separate sets without sharing a song that night. A petition seeking refunds or another performance had passed 1,200 signatures by Sunday, and some concertgoers said an apology would be enough.

Reports have attributed the Atlanta delay to a backstage disagreement over whether to wait for people caught in traffic. Its sources said Usher wanted to begin on time while Brown wanted more ticket holders to reach the stadium first.

But the reason for the SoFi cancellation hasn’t been established. The cancellation notice concerns November 16, and it doesn’t establish that the remaining joint tour dates are being scrapped.

The singers have shared the stage again since that difficult Atlanta opening, including during their Sunday performance.

Their calendar still includes tonight (November 11) before the remaining Southern California date. Their Friday set had already included joint appearances on Back to Sleep and the remix of It Depends.

The next listed stop after SoFi is New Orleans, with Caesars Superdome shows on November 20 and November 21.

item.title: Tyler Perry Says Georgia Remains Home Despite Puerto Rico Move
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Tyler Perry clears up his relocation plans at an Atlanta premiere and explains what stays put as he heads to Puerto Rico.
item.content:encoded:
Tyler Perry isn’t packing up his Georgia studio just because he plans to spend more time in Puerto Rico. He addressed the move at the Atlanta premiere of The Gospel of Christmas on Monday night.

Perry told WSB-TV at the Tabernacle that he expects to work from Puerto Rico for a stretch while keeping his Georgia ties intact.

“The studio will still be here,” Perry said, drawing a distinction between his living arrangements and the business.

“Georgia’s still gonna always be home even though I’ll be living there full-time for a while,” Perry said.

The filmmaker was back in the city celebrating a holiday drama shot primarily in Atlanta.

His role in the state also extends beyond the movies he makes there. Perry recently joined Keisha Lance Bottoms’ Georgia transition team, and the governor-elect attended Monday’s premiere.

Perry said he called Gov. Brian Kemp after Bottoms won the election. He described wanting the outgoing governor to help equip her administration to keep business moving and serve people across Georgia.

The Tabernacle itself carries personal history for Perry, who connected the premiere venue to his early theater career.

He said returning there mattered because it was part of his path after the 14th Street Playhouse.

The new movie puts that faith-centered storytelling alongside a cast filled with singers. Tank and Fantasia Barrino lead a lineup that also includes Fred Hammond, Shirley Caesar, Yolanda Adams and CeCe Winans.

Tank plays Isaac, a pastor trying to rescue a struggling New York church while facing problems within his family and community. Barrino plays Rebecca, with gospel music woven through the fight to keep the church alive.

The Gospel of Christmas begins streaming on Netflix on Wednesday, November 11.
